name: City Museum
unique: A ten story former shoe factory turned into a climbable sculpture of salvaged industrial junk: tunnels, a school bus hanging off the roof and a slide that drops five stories.
buzz: Kids disappear into the tunnels for hours; adults need closed shoes and a tolerance for tight spaces. The rooftop is extra.

name: Kansas City Barbecue Crawl
unique: Burnt ends, sauce dipped ribs and a style built on hickory and a tomato molasses sauce that is sweeter than Texas and thicker than Memphis.
buzz: Joe's Kansas City and Arthur Bryant's are the canonical stops; locals argue about Gates. Order burnt ends and a Big Red.

name: Nelson-Atkins Museum of Art
unique: A free encyclopedic museum with a strong Asian collection, European painting and the giant shuttlecocks on the lawn.
buzz: Free and world class, with a beautiful lawn and a good cafe. The shuttlecocks are the photo.

name: National WWI Museum and Memorial
unique: The national museum of the First World War, with trenches, weapons, personal letters and a tower with a view of the city.
buzz: One of the best war museums in the country, and the tower is worth the climb. Allow three hours.

name: Forest Park
unique: A 1,300 acre park larger than Central Park, holding the zoo, the art museum, the science center, a lake and miles of trails, most of them free.
buzz: You can spend a whole day here without paying admission. The boathouse and the art museum are the anchors.

name: Missouri Botanical Garden
unique: A 79 acre garden with a Victorian conservatory, a Japanese garden, a climatron dome and an extensive orchid collection.
buzz: The Climatron and the Japanese garden are the highlights. Spring and fall are the best seasons.

name: St. Louis Zoo
unique: One of the last great free zoos, with a walk through penguin house, a grizzly exhibit and a 1904 Flight Cage from the World's Fair.
buzz: Free admission and genuinely good exhibits; parking costs more than most zoos' entry. Go at opening.

name: Wonders of Wildlife
unique: A massive wildlife museum and aquarium with sharks, otters, a swamp, a cave and mounted animals from around the world.
buzz: Bigger and better than expected, with live animals and a real aquarium. Allow half a day.

name: Silver Dollar City
unique: An 1880s-themed park built over a natural cave, with craftsmen blowing glass and forging iron between world class coasters like Outlaw Run.
buzz: The theming is genuinely charming and the coasters are excellent; Christmas lights are a regional pilgrimage. Branson traffic is real.

name: Arabia Steamboat Museum
unique: Cargo from a steamboat that sank in 1856, recovered intact from a cornfield, with tools, dishes, clothing and food still preserved.
buzz: The everyday objects are the fascinating part, and the recovery story is improbable. Good for kids.

name: Cathedral Basilica of Saint Louis
unique: A Romanesque cathedral with the largest mosaic collection in the world, 41 million pieces covering the ceiling in gold and color.
buzz: The mosaics are astonishing and it is free. Go on a weekday for quiet.

name: Ha Ha Tonka
unique: A stone castle ruin on a bluff above the Lake of the Ozarks, with a spring, a natural bridge and a waterfall in a dolomite canyon.
buzz: The castle ruin is eerier and more beautiful than expected; the spring trail is a steep stair climb. Sunset is the time.

name: Gateway Arch
unique: A 630-foot stainless steel catenary arch with a tram that squeezes you into a pod and lifts you to a window the size of a shoebox over the Mississippi.
buzz: The tram is claustrophobic and the view is worth it; the museum underneath is excellent and free. Book timed tickets.

name: Ozark Float Trip
unique: A Missouri institution: a raft, a cooler and a slow river through Ozark hills, with gravel bars for stopping and no schedule at all.
buzz: The Huzzah and Current rivers are the classics; weekends get rowdy and the water is cold. Book the shuttle and bring a dry bag.

name: Lemp Mansion
unique: A brewery family's mansion where several members died by suicide, now a restaurant and inn with ghost tours, dinner theater and overnight rooms that guests leave early.
buzz: The dinner mystery is campy and the history is genuinely tragic; overnight guests report doors and footsteps. Book the tour before you commit to a room.

name: Anheuser-Busch Brewery Tour
unique: A tour of the historic brewery with the red brick buildings, the Clydesdale stables and a tasting at the end.
buzz: The Clydesdales are the highlight and the tour is free. Book ahead and bring ID.

name: Crown Candy Kitchen
unique: A 1913 soda fountain and sandwich counter in a north city neighborhood, famous for a five pound milkshake challenge and a bacon sandwich that defeats most people.
buzz: The malts are the real draw and the heart attack burger is a stunt; the line moves and the neighborhood is worth supporting.

name: Hermann Wine Trail
unique: A Missouri River town settled by German immigrants, with a brick main street and a cluster of wineries along the valley.
buzz: The wines are sweet and the town is charming. Book a designated driver or a shuttle.

name: Mark Twain Boyhood Home
unique: The house where Samuel Clemens grew up, with the whitewashed fence, the museum and the river town that became Tom Sawyer's St. Petersburg.
buzz: For readers it is a pilgrimage, and the town leans into it. The fence painting is a photo op for kids.

name: Missouri State Capitol
unique: A limestone capitol above the Missouri River with a mural by Thomas Hart Benton in the lounge and a museum on the first floor.
buzz: The Benton mural is the reason art people stop and the view from the river steps is the photograph; tours are free.

name: Table Rock Lake
unique: A clear Ozark lake with coves, marinas, swimming and bass fishing, next to the Branson strip but a world away.
buzz: The lake is the quiet alternative to the shows, with good swimming and rental boats.

name: Union Station
unique: A 1914 Beaux Arts train station with a grand hall, a science center, a planetarium and a model train gallery.
buzz: The grand hall is the photo and the model trains are the kid draw. Free to walk through.

name: Patee House Museum
customer: History families, Pony Express fans, road trippers
unique: A 1858 hotel that was the Pony Express headquarters, now a museum with a railroad, a stagecoach and a recreation of a frontier main street.
buzz: The street scene and the Pony Express story are the reasons to come; it is old fashioned and good with children.

name: St. Charles Main Street
unique: A brick main street of 1800s buildings on the Missouri, the first state capital and the start of the Lewis and Clark trail, with a riverfront park.
buzz: The street and the Katy Trail trailhead are the two reasons to come and the shops are touristy; the fall festival is the local event.

name: Fantastic Caverns
unique: The only cave in the country you tour by jeep drawn tram, riding through a underground river passage without leaving your seat.
buzz: The ride is the reason children love it and the cave is accessible for people who cannot walk far; the tour is about an hour.

name: Rockcliffe Mansion
customer: House tour people, history fans, families
unique: A 30 room mansion on a bluff above the Mississippi, with original furnishings and a view over Hannibal, left empty for decades and restored.
buzz: The house and the river view are the tour and the story of its abandonment is the interest; it pairs with the Mark Twain sites.

name: Meramec Caverns
unique: A five story cavern lit in neon, billed on barn roofs for a hundred miles, with a sound and light show and a Jesse James outlaw legend.
buzz: It is unabashedly old school roadside Americana; the formations are impressive and the show is kitsch. Kids love it.

name: Museum of Art and Archaeology
unique: A university museum with ancient Greek pottery, a mummy and American painting, free in a building on the Columbia campus.
buzz: The ancient collection is the surprise and the museum is free; it is small and the campus is a pleasant walk.

name: Jefferson Landing
unique: A restored 1850s river landing with a store and a house built into the levee, where the Santa Fe Trail trade began.
buzz: The buildings and the river view are the stop and it is free; the levee wall itself is the interesting engineering.

name: Jesse James Home
customer: Outlaw history fans, families, road trippers
unique: The small house where Jesse James was shot in 1882, with the bullet hole in the wall and the story of how his widow sold tours.
buzz: The house is small and the bullet hole is the artifact; it is a quick stop next to the Patee House.
